extracted.intended_audience: business news readers, investors, and financial journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing a business-news article announcing a company withdrawing or postponing an IPO filing, covering the core facts, company statements, background, valuation context, and any subsequent corporate actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Points summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise 'Key Points' bullet list at the top summarizing the main facts of the story (e.g., decision to withdraw S-1, reason to postpone IPO, related executive change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short bullets to surface the essential takeaways for readers who skim. Include the primary action (withdraw/postpone), immediate context (investor roadshow delay, weak demand), and notable follow-ups (executive resignations or plans to revisit markets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear headline and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Prominently display a clear headline about the action (e.g., 'WeWork pulls IPO filing') and show publication and update timestamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timestamps (published and updated) signal recency and whether material has changed — important for fast-moving financial news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph with the main event
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with a lead that states the central news item (the company will withdraw its S-1 filing and postpone its IPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should answer who, what, and why (briefly). Follow with succinct expansion in the next paragraph(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct company statement and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotes from the company and identify speakers by name and title (e.g., co-CEOs Artie Minson and Sebastian Gunningham said in a statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use verbatim quotes for the company's public position ('We have decided to postpone our IPO ...') and clearly attribute them; this provides an authoritative source and balances third-party reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background and chronology
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a short timeline and background (when the S-1 was filed, investor roadshow delay, prior announcements like CEO resignation) to contextualize the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key prior events that led to the development so readers understand causation and recent history; mention dates and prior actions explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation and market reaction context
rubrics_metrics.description: Report valuation figures and investor sentiment (private-market valuation assigned by backers, public investors' attempted valuations, and skepticism following disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present notable numbers (e.g., private $47 billion vs. public investor estimates as low as $10 billion) and describe how those valuations influenced market perception and the IPO's prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report operational/cost-cutting steps and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe steps the company is taking to address problems (e.g., selling assets, cutting costs, potential layoffs) and connect them to the IPO outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reported actions (sell private jet, put side businesses up for sale, potential layoffs of up to one-third of workers) and explain that such steps are framed as efforts 'to get the company back on track for an IPO.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and linking to reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite and link to other outlets or reports used as sources (e.g., Business Insider, The Information) and make clear what information came from those sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing external reporting, attribute the specific claim to the outlet and, where possible, link to the original story. Distinguish between company statements and third-party reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and update transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a correction or update note when the story changes or when earlier reporting needs clarification (e.g., updated to reflect which outlets reported which facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what was corrected or updated and why (which publication reported what). Timestamp corrections/updates to maintain transparency and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia and additional reporting hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed or link to related multimedia (videos, live segments) and related coverage to give readers more ways to consume and follow the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include video clips or links to live coverage (e.g., 'WATCH LIVE' or embedded video segments) and label them with runtime; these items complement the text and can provide expert commentary or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader engagement and newsroom housekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ways for readers to engage (news tips, newsletters, subscriptions) and include licensing/reprints and contact information as standard site footer content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not part of the core news narrative, including 'Got a confidential news tip?' or 'Subscribe to CNBC PRO' and licensing details is standard practice for distribution and audience development.
